description: TicTacToe — 3x3 perfect-info zero-sum game. 2 players alternate placing X/O. Win by 3-in-a-row (horizontal/vertical/diagonal). Used as a D-067 Phase C *negative control*: physis hints are expected to either (a) reproduce known optimal play with no learning curve, or (b) accumulate trivial confidence with no transfer value. The contrast against Avalon's positive bracket isolates which game-shape features make physis substrate useful.

partial_observability.note: Perfect information game — no per-agent filtering. Both players see the full board state at all times.

state_space.trace_recommendation: Single board state per turn; ~9 lines max per match. Trace is small enough to retain ground-truth always.

action_set.constraints: 0 <= row <= 2 AND 0 <= col <= 2 AND board[row][col] is null

terminal.ground_truth: scores[agent_id] = 1.0 if won, 0.5 if draw, 0.0 if lost

intermediate_per_turn.ground_truth: 0.0 every turn — no per-move reward signal
intermediate_per_turn.shape: Sparse — terminal-only by design. Phase C negative-control hypothesis: the absence of intermediate signal contributes to physis's expected null-effect on this field.

distill_prompt_addendum:
## Field-specific calibration for TicTacToe

**This match's `episode_id`: `{episode_id}`** — use this exact string as the `last_episode` value on every hint you emit.

TicTacToe is a *solved* perfect-information zero-sum game. The optimal policy is known (center → corner → block forks → fork creation). Phase B v3 retrieval matches `precondition` against a fixed *state_signature* dict the engine emits per turn. Use ONLY the precondition keys below, with values from the listed enums. Do NOT invent new keys — they will not be visible to retrieval.

Allowed precondition keys + value enums:

```yaml
my_mark:           X | O                          # your mark this match
move_number:       1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9   # current move (1-indexed)
center_open:       true | false                   # is [1,1] still empty
corners_taken_band: none | one | two | three_or_four  # how many corners are occupied
opponent_threat:   none | single | double         # opponent's longest existing line (1, 2, 3-in-row in single-line)
my_threat:         none | single | double         # your longest existing line
```

Omit any key you don't want to constrain.

## YAML output shape

Emit a single top-level `hints:` key. Each hint has `_hint_type: action` (TicTacToe has no peer talk; rhetorical hints don't apply — omit them).

Example (skeleton):

```yaml
hints:
  - id: <slug>
    _hint_type: action
    rule: "<one-line if-then>"
    precondition:
      move_number: 1
      center_open: true
    action:
      type: place
      position: [1, 1]
    confidence: tentative
    evidence:
      confirmed: <count>
      disconfirmed: <count>
    last_episode: {episode_id}
```

If no new hint surfaces this match (e.g. you played the optimal known policy and there's nothing new to learn), emit an empty `hints: []` block — that itself is data for the Phase C negative-control bracket.

prior_art_anchors.import_target: Reference for what physis hints *should* converge to in the limit — and observation that this convergence carries no transfer value to non-solved games.
